note: Pre-registered per the price-action design study. Round-number grids fixed in advance (US30/NAS100/DE40=500, US500=100), never swept. Prior-low windows EXCLUDE the entry bar (including it makes distance trivially zero on every new low, which is exactly when IBS<0.2 fires).

H2_approached_vs_breached.verdict: no effect - and the sign is OPPOSITE to the folklore: trades that had already breached the level did BETTER

near_vs_far_filter.verdict: the near/far split looks appealing but is not statistically distinguishable (H1 p=0.487); filtering to 'near' would DISCARD 109.5R of profit to gain 0.12 mean R on the half retained

conclusion: SUPPORT/RESISTANCE ADDS NO MEASURABLE EDGE to this book. All four distance measures test flat (|rho| <= 0.06, every p > 0.16). This matches the design study's stated prior and the published record: Osler's order-clustering effects are real but pip-scale and decay within ~2 hours, while this is a multi-day swing book on CFDs; and every standalone technical-level rule tested in the literature (Sullivan/Timmermann/White 1999, Bajgrowicz/Scaillet 2012) lost its edge once data-snooping and costs were handled. Recorded as a REJECTION so it is never re-tested by accident.
